subject: CheshirePay performance escalation: payment timeouts & error surge
messages:
From: Alice Deng <alice@cheshirepay.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-20T08:12:00Z
Subject: Payment timeouts and 500 surge - urgent

Jordan / team —

We're seeing a sudden spike in 500s and timeouts from Redwood for our payment validation calls across EU and US regions starting ~08:00Z. Error rate jumped from ~0.6% to ~7.8% and median p95 latency went from 190ms to ~1.9s. This is causing payment retries and downstream queuing — we're blocking new checkouts. Attached is a short log sample and our trace ids.

Can you confirm you've seen this and provide ETA for mitigation? We need an executive update for our CTO in the next 30–45 minutes.

Attachment: cheshire-500-sample.log (txt)

— Alice
Head of Platform, CheshirePay

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Deng <alice@cheshirepay.com>
Date: 2027-06-20T08:23:00Z
Subject: Re: Payment timeouts and 500 surge - urgent

Quick triage update from the ops side (initial):
- Confirmed the error spike and latency increase across two model variants (q4_8 and q8_0) starting ~08:00Z.
- Rolled a hotfix route: routing ~30% of traffic to the non-quantized variant (fallback) to reduce OOM/retry churn. Initial telemetry shows error rate dropping to ~2.4% in the fallback cohort.
- Started horizontal scaling on Dedicated pool for CheshirePay (added 6 GPUs) — ongoing; should be effective within 8–10 minutes.
- Captured initial metrics dump and put on shared drive.

What we need from Marcus: root-cause hypothesis + whether a roll-back of current quantized build is required.

Attachment: initial-metrics-20270620.csv
War-room (Slack): https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C12345/p1624326000000200

— Mina
Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Deng <alice@cheshirepay.com>
Date: 2027-06-20T08:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Payment timeouts and 500 surge - urgent

Technical update / preliminary root cause: 
- Hypothesis: an interaction between the recent KV-cache invalidation change in q4_8 quantized runtime and our memory accounting on the Dedicated instance class. Under typical load the runtime is fine, but under the specific token distribution for CheshirePay's validation payloads we've observed cascading OOMs leading to automatic retries and elevated latency.
- Evidence: increased mem alloc failures correlated with the spike (see heap dump summary).
- Immediate mitigations applied: fallback routing (Mina), horizontal scale (Mina), and setting aggressive circuit-breaker thresholds for payment routes to prevent retry storms.
- Next steps (timeline):
  * 0–10m: current mitigations — monitor.
  * 10–60m: revert the KV-cache invalidation change for the q4_8 binary and re-deploy canary.
  * 60–180m: full verification, progressive re-roll.

Customer-facing ask: we should offer a short customer note with the current status, actions we've taken, and expected ETA for resolution (~1–3 hours to full stabilization depending on canary results).

Attachment: heapdump-summary.txt
Jira: https://jira.redwood.com/browse/INF-3947

— Marcus
Tech Lead, Inference Infrastructure
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Deng <alice@cheshirepay.com>
Date: 2027-06-20T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Payment timeouts and 500 surge - urgent

Jordan / Mina — draft executive readout for CheshirePay below. Please review and sign off; Jordan will send to Alice once we have approvals.

[Executive Readout — CheshirePay incident, 2027-06-20]
Summary: At ~08:00Z we observed a burst of 500 errors and elevated p95 latency impacting payment validation flows for CheshirePay. The root cause is a regression in the q4_8 quantized runtime interacting with the KV-cache invalidation logic causing memory allocation failures and retries.
Actions taken so far:
- Routed 30% of traffic to the non-quantized fallback variant to immediately reduce error surface.
- Scaled Dedicated capacity (+6 GPUs) and set circuit-breaker limits to reduce retry amplification.
- Engineering will revert the problematic KV-cache change and deploy a canary within 1 hour.
Estimated impact and ETA:
- Partial stabilization observed in fallback traffic (error rate ~2.4%).
- Tentative ETA for canary and progressive re-roll: 1–3 hours; full verification within 3 hours.
Next steps / commitments:
- We will provide an hourly update for the next 3 hours and a postmortem within 72 hours.
- If rollback canary looks good, we will re-enable quantized variant after verifying memory metrics for 30 minutes.

Please reply-all with any wording changes. Jordan, ready for you to send once Mina and Marcus confirm the timeline wording.

— Laura
VP, Sales — Enterprise Accounts, Redwood Inference
